| Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |

| Layout | Current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
| napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets and builds only the packages in the release. |
| Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
| Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |

Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:

- A multi-registry release is not atomic.
- Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Go and NuGet publishers are not available.

Package owners control native lifecycle hooks. Callisto invokes supported tools without rewriting those hooks. See [publishing](publishing.md) for credentials and Python index limits, and [releasing](releasing.md) for the complete operation and recovery rules.
# Stability

What Callisto promises to keep working from 1.0, and what it does not. A breaking change to anything in the first table needs a major version.

## Stable

| Surface | The promise |
| --- | --- |
| The eight commands (`add`, `status`, `version`, `pre`, `snapshot`, `init`, `release`, `completions`) and their flags | A flag keeps its meaning; a new flag never changes what the command did without it. |
| Exit codes | `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error. |
| `--format json` reports | Every report carries `schemaVersion`. Within a version a field is not removed, renamed or retyped; fields may be added. A shape change bumps the version. |
| `callisto.toml` | A key keeps its meaning. Unknown keys are an error, so a new key arrives in a minor release and never changes an existing file's behavior. |
| Changesets | The `.changeset/*.md` format and `pre.json` stay compatible with `@changesets/cli` for npm names; other ecosystems use `ecosystem/name` keys. |
| Error codes | A code keeps naming the same condition and is never reused. New codes may appear. |
| Tag names | `{name}@{version}` by default, `ecosystem/name@{version}` once another ecosystem has a package of that name. Pin a name with `tag-template` if a stable tag matters to your tooling. |
| The GitHub Actions | The inputs of `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto`. The floating `v1` tag moves only on stable releases; pin a commit for a fixed version. |

## CI plumbing

The generated workflows use `release plan`, `release inspect`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release build-python`, `release-pr`, `matrix`, `compose-pr-body` and `schema`. They are hidden from `--help` and work only with the same Callisto version that generated them: the intent, decision, receipt and run envelope carry versions, and a reader rejects any other. Keep the action and the binary on one version, and regenerate with `callisto init` after an upgrade.

## Not covered

- Text output, stderr, warnings and the wording of error messages.
- The library crates (`callisto-model`, `-manifests`, `-graph`). They are internal and version in lockstep with the CLI.
- The order of keys in JSON output, and timing or performance.
- Platforms without a published binary. Windows is not supported.
# Configuration reference

Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).

This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.

## Top-level tables

| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |

For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli"]
```

## Identity and defaults

Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). content.content:
1 │ # Releasing
  2 │ 
  3 │ How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.
  4 │ 
  5 │ For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).
  6 │ 
  7 │ ---
  8 │ 
  9 │ ## Local release: `callisto release`
 10 │ 
 11 │ `callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
 12 │ 
 13 │ - `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
 14 │ - `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
 15 │ - It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
 16 │ - It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
 17 │ - It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
 18 │ - A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.
 19 │ 
 20 │ `cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.
 21 │ 
 22 │ A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.
 23 │ 
 24 │ ### Current retry limit
 25 │ 
 26 │ If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.
 27 │ 
 28 │ - `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
 29 │ - Generated simple workflows share this limit.
 30 │ - CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.
 31 │ 
 32 │ ---
 33 │ 
 34 │ ## Generated workflows
 35 │ 
 36 │ `callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.
 37 │ 
 38 │ Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.
 39 │ 
 40 │ - **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
 41 │ - **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
 42 │ - Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
 43 │ 
 44 │ Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).
 45 │ 
 46 │ Generated build support has these boundaries:
 47 │ 
 48 │ - Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
 49 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
 50 │ - Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
 51 │ - Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
 52 │ 
 53 │ The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
 54 │ 
 55 │ Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.
 56 │ 
 57 │ Build-matrix limits:
 58 │ 
 59 │ - An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
 60 │ - Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
 61 │ - Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
 62 │ - The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
 63 │ - Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.
 64 │ 
 65 │ ---
 66 │ 
 67 │ ## Release PR and approval
 68 │ 
 69 │ The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.
 70 │ 
 71 │ The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
 72 │

 89 │ Every release run records two different revisions:

102 │ ## Finding releases that did not finish
103 │ 
104 │ `callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. 111 │ 
112 │ Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

114 │ ## A stale release PR
115 │ 
116 │ Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. 120 │ ## Recovering an older release
121 │ 
122 │ Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
123 │ 
124 │ **E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
125 │ 
126 │ ```sh
127 │ SHA=<release-source sha>
128 │ git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
129 │ git push origin "<tag>"
130 │ gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
131 │ ```
132 │ 
133 │ **`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:
134 │ 
135 │ ```sh
136 │ gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset

138 │ ```

140 │ ## Publication checks
141 │ 
142 │ Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
143 │ 
144 │ Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. 145 │ 
146 │ GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
147 │ 
148 │ ---
149 │

151 │

2 │ 3 │

4 │ 5 │ --- 6 │ 7 │ ## Invariants 8 │ 9 │ 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 10 │ 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 11 │ 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST. String-only `package.json` changes replace scanned literal spans in the original text; other changes keep key order and fingerprinted indentation and line endings. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 12 │ 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 13 │ 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 14 │ 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group).   9 │ ## First publish
 10 │ 
 11 │ A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:
 12 │ 
 13 │ - **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.
 14 │ - **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
 15 │ - **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
 16 │ - **Package managers.** An npm package is published with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), passing `--tag`, `--access` and, where the manager takes one, `--registry`. Yarn takes no `--registry`; it reads `publishConfig.registry` from the package itself.
 17 │ - **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
 18 │ - **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.
 19 │ 
 20 │ ## Pulling a release
 21 │ 
 22 │ Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:
 23 │ 
 24 │ | Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
 25 │ | --- | --- | --- |
 26 │ | crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
 27 │ | npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. A used version number can never be reused, and removing every version blocks the name for 24 hours. |
 28 │ | PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |
 29 │ 
 30 │ Registries cache their indexes for minutes, so a pulled version can keep appearing briefly. Prefer the soft pull, then release a fixed, higher version through the normal flow. Leave the git tag in place: Callisto treats an existing tag as a release already made. Yanking does not undo a leaked secret; rotate it.
 31 │ 
 32 │ If you remove a version that is still the manifest version, `callisto release` will try to finish it again and stop with an error. Bump the version with a changeset instead.
 33 │ 
 34 │ See the registries' own pages for current rules: [cargo yank](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html), [npm unpublish](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish) and the [PyPI help](https://pypi.org/help/).
 35 │ 
 36 │ ## Where a publish goes
 37 │ 
 38 │ A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. Set `url` on the registry entry to pin the destination in `callisto.toml`.

 40 │ ---
 41 │ 
 42 │ ## npm
 43 │ 
 44 │ Two supported patterns.
 45 │ 
 46 │ ### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
 47 │ 
 48 │ Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
 49 │ 
 50 │ ```yaml
 51 │ - name: Authenticate with npm registry
 52 │   run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
 53 │   env:
 54 │     NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
 55 │ 
 56 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
 57 │ ```
 58 │ 
 59 │ `npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
 60 │ 
 61 │ ### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
 62 │ 
 63 │ `actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
 64 │ 
 65 │ ```yaml
 66 │ - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
 67 │   with:
 68 │     node-version: '20'
 69 │     registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
 70 │ 
 71 │ - run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
 72 │   env:
 73 │     NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
 74 │ ```
 75 │ 
 76 │ `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
 77 │ 
 78 │ ### Choosing a pattern
 79 │ 
 80 │ | Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
 81 │ | --- | --- | --- |
 82 │ | Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
 83 │ | Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
 84 │ | Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
 85 │ | Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
 86 │ 
 87 │ ### Provenance
 88 │ 
 89 │ Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
 90 │ 
 91 │ ---
 92 │ 
 93 │ ## Cargo (crates.io)
 94 │ 
 95 │ Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
 96 │ 
 97 │ ```yaml
 98 │ env:
 99 │   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
100 │ ```
101 │ 
102 │ Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.
103 │ 
104 │ ---
105 │ 
106 │ ## Python (PyPI)
107 │ 
108 │ Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
109 │ 
110 │ ```yaml
111 │ env:
112 │   TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
113 │   TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
114 │ ```
115 │ 
116 │ Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
117 │ 
118 │ The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.
119 │ 
120 │ ### Generated Callisto workflows
121 │ 
122 │ Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
123 │ 
124 │ Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.
125 │ 
126 │ ### Current Python support limits
127 │ 
128 │ Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
129 │ 
130 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
131 │ - Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
132 │ - A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
133 │ - A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
134 │ - A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
135 │ - A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
136 │ - Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
137 │ - `release` refuses snapshot versions (E169), so a snapshot is never published. Python snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI would reject anyway. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
# Architecture decision records

- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.
- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — proposed v1 model with some behavior already implemented. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.

## Rules

- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.
- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.
# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. The evidence is in `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- System findings and verification limits: `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

128 │ Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
129 │ 
130 │ - Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
131 │ - Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
132 │ - A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
133 │ - A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
134 │ - A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
135 │ - A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
136 │ - Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
137 │ - `release` refuses snapshot versions (E169), so a snapshot is never published. Python snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI would reject anyway. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
# Architecture decision records

- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
- [11. # 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. The evidence is in `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: partly implemented. Canonical references, derived release ownership, per-distribution publish ordering, registry-before-tag ordering, PyPI file-set completion, platform packages before their owner, the `publish-url` split and prerelease npm dist-tags are current behavior ([ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md)). Co-located Cargo/Maturin version derivation, build-input relationships, authenticated private PyPI, npm dist-tag promotion and the Go and NuGet adapters are design only. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Remaining work is in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release owner is derived from existing types and sealed by the intent digest; no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.

## Canonical references and migration

- Configuration, generated config, machine reports and command-line arguments use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names, resolved when read, because an entry names an owner package and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli`. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names, and a `pypi/` reference uses the declared name.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- A bare name in a changeset or `pre.json` resolves through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Persisted release documents are already canonical-only.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force, including its default tag `{display id}@{version}`, which [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) keeps. Do not rename existing tags to canonicalize selectors; a native rename is declared with `previous-tag-templates`.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. Co-located Cargo/Maturin is after v1; today it fails with E007, and separate-directory Cargo and Python packages are supported. The design for it: Cargo is the version authority and the Python distribution uses `dynamic = ["version"]`. Maturin does not map versions; it parses the Cargo version as PEP 440, so Callisto computes the expected Python version with the `pep440_rs` crate and verifies the built metadata. Several SemVer prereleases are not faithful in PEP 440 (`pre`, `c` and `rc` collapse to `rc`; `dev` and `post` change the sort order; `+build` is a local version PyPI rejects), so accept only stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N` and refuse the rest, and snapshots, before any write. Refuse a static Python version beside Cargo, which maturin does not check. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter or arbitrary SCM-derived backends.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

# Road to v1

Unshipped work only. [Owner requirement](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md), [scoped model and prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Canonical `ecosystem/name` references, historical tag ownership, one tag and release per package, per-distribution publish ordering and the redacted failure tail have shipped. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) records them.

## Scope and guardrails

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI, including napi-rs layouts. Co-located Cargo/Maturin is after v1; separate-directory Cargo and Python packages are supported. Go and NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Native tools and CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform or cross-registry transaction.
- Committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only `execute` receives registry secrets; the repo has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate.
- Each implementation PR updates the affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic.

## Open work

| Item | State |
| --- | --- |
| Co-located Cargo/Maturin | After v1. Both a static and a dynamic Python version fail with E007. |
| Production-path registry tests for Cargo and PyPI | The tests drive the publisher argv directly and bypass registry binding and observation. A path through binding is blocked because `registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https URLs, loopback included. Decide the approach, then build it or drop it. npm already goes through the real adapter. |
| Native fixture evidence | Cargo and napi clean install and load, mixed workspaces and packed pnpm metadata are not recorded as a verification matrix. |
| First-release onboarding time | The goal of under ten minutes from a fresh repo to a first published release has not been measured. |
| Release target table | `matrix.rs` carries its own 18-triple table instead of reading rustc's target facts. |

## Owner decisions still open

- Private and HTML-only PyPI indexes: [publishing](../publishing.md) says they need explicit support.
- npm channel promotion. Prereleases already publish under their own dist-tag.
- Universal checksums, and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only releases in managed CI: `status` warns, but whether inference may open the release PR is an ADR 2 question.
- Release-commit provenance: ADR 2 documents the unkeyed digest.
- Whether to add a workspace-wide check for discarded source errors. The lints deny `let_underscore_must_use`, `let_underscore_untyped` and `map_err_ignore`.
- npm JSON layout normalization, and the scope of napi `.node` attestation.
- External items: rust-cache pin, bot-PR check policy, token rotation and the retired-crate migration notices.

## After 1.0

OIDC trusted publishing ([plan](OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md)), `cargo-semver-checks` on the promised surfaces (schema output, config and report formats), and a review of the remaining `expect` calls.

# 5. System git only

Status: Accepted (implemented in #145)

## Context

- Callisto reads commits, tags and staged changes, and creates and pushes tags.
- From 2026-08-03 `callisto-vcs` had two backends behind `GitDataSource`: native gix (`GitRepository`) and a shell fallback (`ShellGit`), with reads retrying through the shell on any native error (commit bb2a69cc4).
- The CLI already required a `git` binary: trust observation, staged changes and every fallback went through it (#145).

## Decision

Every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the user's `git` through `CommandRunner`. `callisto_model::vcs` has one Git access type, `GitAccess`, and defines no backend trait; `GitAccess` implements callisto-model's `CommitWalker` for severity inference (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`). Git operations use the user's git config and identity, except release tags: with no identity set, the target commit's committer becomes the tagger, and `TagSignPolicy::ForceUnsigned` adds `--no-sign` (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`). Workspace-root discovery looks for a `.git` entry on disk (`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs`).

## Options considered

- **gix as the primary backend with a shell fallback (two backends)** — rejected in #145: "Two backends meant two semantics to keep in step (gix ignored TagSignPolicy) and 106 extra crates." The changeset adds: "every Git read and write already had to work through the `git` binary the CLI requires."
- **gix only** — not considered in #145. Reason not recorded.

## Consequences

- History walks use `git log --no-merges --full-history`, matching the gix commit sets; plain `git log` history simplification drops commits whose change a later merge discarded.
- Callisto depends on the installed git version and parses its output.
- Annotated tags work on runners with no git identity: the tagger falls back to the target commit's committer (#145).
- The managed release-PR action is outside this decision: it writes its commit and branch refs through the GitHub API (`.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`).
- Today `release-pr commit-plan` reads staged bytes from the worktree, not the index (as of 0.10.2; `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`, v1 fix plan §1).

## Enforcement

- `callisto_model::vcs` has no gix dependency and one `GitAccess` type (`crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs`).
- Nothing bans gix in `deny.toml`; reintroducing it needs a new ADR.

## Revisit when

- A required Git operation is impossible or unacceptably slow through the binary, measured against the #145 numbers.
- Callisto must run where no `git` binary exists.

## Sources

- PR #145 (7ad333311): commit body, PR body, `.changeset/calm-foxes-pounce.md`
- Commit bb2a69cc4 (two-backend `GitDataSource` introduced)
- docs/00-design.md §15 `callisto-vcs` entry, describing the pre-#145 two-backend design (`git show 7ad333311^:docs/00-design.md`)
# 6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension

Status: Accepted (implemented in #142)

## Context

- Callisto started moon-first. docs/02-library-vs-moon-decision.md chose "Option C": a moon-free core, with a moon WASM extension (`callisto-moon`) as the single reference integration next to the CLI. The core had to build for `wasm32-wasip1` and pass fixtures under wasmtime.
- The Track 0 spike (ffc922d44, 2026-08-04) tested gix inside a WASI guest. `gix-ref` worked, but `gix-odb` and `gix-pack` read objects through mmap, which WASI rejects with ENOSYS. Verdict NO-GO: the extension had to run `git` on the host through moon's `warpgate_pdk::exec_command`.
- moon's project-graph edges carry no version requirement, so moon could never drive the cascade; it could only locate projects and cross-check edges (docs/02 change 1 and 2).

## Decision

Callisto ships one native binary (crates.io, GitHub release archives, the `setup-callisto` action). For proto and moon users, a proto TOML plugin (`proto/callisto.toml`) installs that binary from the GitHub release assets, and moon tasks call it like any tool. There is no moon WASM extension and no WASM build. The core's only moon awareness is treating a `.moon/` directory as a workspace-root marker and skipping it during discovery (`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs`, `ignore_walk.rs`).

## Options considered

- **moon WASM extension (`callisto-moon`)** — removed in #142. What it duplicated or forced:
  - A second command surface: `execute_extension` dispatched `status` and `release` inside WASM (`git show f8598d19e^:crates/callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs`).
  - Moon-only seams in the core: `ProjectLocator::declared_edges`, `DeclaredEdge`, the `GraphEdgeDisagreement` cross-check, `IdentityResolver` (E155, E156) and wasm32-gated fallbacks in `callisto-vcs`; in the CLI, `--strict-graph` and the `wrapper` feature.
  - A second release artifact (`callisto-moon.wasm`) and installer (`setup-callisto-wasm`).
  - wasmtime in the dependency tree through `moon_pdk_test_utils → extism → wasmtime`. `deny.toml` carried 18 advisory ignores for the moon extension's dependencies, 17 of them through wasmtime. A new wasmtime advisory blocked CI on every open PR (fc3db408d).
- **moon-first core (Option A)** — rejected in docs/02: knope's cascade is trapped in its binary and Nx needed a v21 rewrite after coordination logic leaked into per-ecosystem plugins.

## Consequences

- #142: Cargo.lock 810 → 365 packages; `cargo deny` needs no advisory ignores.
- moon workspaces get the same binary as everyone else; project discovery is callisto's own walk (`IgnoreWalkLocator`). The proto plugin covers macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (glibc, musl) only.
- The proto plugin cannot verify checksums until releases publish `.sha256` assets (#142 follow-up).

## Enforcement

- `.github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh` (run by `just ci` through `workflow-contracts`) fails if the release build accepts the old `callisto-moon.wasm` tuple.
- The same test also rejects a `wasm32-wasip1` CLI tuple. No crate or CI job builds for `wasm32-wasip1`, and nothing checks that.

## Revisit when

- moon offers something a CLI task cannot get (for example project-graph data with version requirements) and the owner wants it.
- WASI gains mmap, or gix-odb gains a read fallback. Git access is shell-only anyway (ADR 5), so this alone is not enough.

## Sources

- PR #142 (2c649a147; f8598d19e, f87aa1f4d, 5988c10cd, 1b0e7e1da), `.changeset/moon-proto-plugin.md`
- Commit ffc922d44 (Track 0 spike)
- docs/02-library-vs-moon-decision.md and docs/00-design.md §0.1 (`git show 11038b11b^:docs/<file>`)
- `git show f8598d19e^:crates/callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs` (extension command dispatch)
- Commit fc3db408d (#38, wasmtime advisory blocking CI); `git show f8598d19e^:deny.toml`
# 9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated

Status: Accepted (implemented in #154)

## Context

- A rerun adopts effects that already landed (ADR 3), so it must decide whether an existing tag is the one it planned.
- The local check read the tag with `git for-each-ref` and compared the target commit and the annotation text. The remote check uses `git ls-remote`, which returns the tag object and peeled commit but not the annotation text, so it compared only the commit.
- The same repository state could therefore be adopted or rejected depending on whether the remote tag had been fetched.

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.
- **Keep the split (text locally, commit remotely)** — rejected: the outcome depends on fetch state.

## Consequences

- Local and remote checks agree.
- A tag with a different message is adopted. The receipt records only the peeled commit (`ProviderEvidenceV1::GitTag { peeled_commit }` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs`), and `gh release create --verify-tag` checks only that the tag exists.

## Enforcement

- Tests in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs` for local and remote observation (different annotation text is adopted; lightweight and other-commit tags conflict).
- REL-RERUN-02 and REL-RERUN-03 in `docs/specs/release.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something downstream starts reading the annotation text (release notes, signing policy, provenance).

## Sources

- Owner decision, `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- The fix in this PR: "fix: stop comparing tag annotation text in release rerun observation"

- The local check read the tag with `git for-each-ref` and compared the target commit and the annotation text. The remote check uses `git ls-remote`, which returns the tag object and peeled commit but not the annotation text, so it compared only the commit.
- The same repository state could therefore be adopted or rejected depending on whether the remote tag had been fetched.

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.
- **Keep the split (text locally, commit remotely)** — rejected: the outcome depends on fetch state.

## Consequences

- Local and remote checks agree.
- A tag with a different message is adopted. The receipt records only the peeled commit (`ProviderEvidenceV1::GitTag { peeled_commit }` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs`), and `gh release create --verify-tag` checks only that the tag exists.

## Enforcement

- Tests in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs` for local and remote observation (different annotation text is adopted; lightweight and other-commit tags conflict).
- REL-RERUN-02 and REL-RERUN-03 in `docs/specs/release.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something downstream starts reading the annotation text (release notes, signing policy, provenance).

## Sources

- Owner decision, `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- The fix in this PR: "fix: stop comparing tag annotation text in release rerun observation"
